rounds.text: Stanbik Agro Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 10 alongside a price-to-book ratio of just 1.31x on a book value of ₹ 25.0 [E1, E2]. The underlying operational performance demonstrates exceptional momentum, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 63% and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 62% [E14, E16]. Profitability metrics consistently outperform sector benchmarks, with a filed ROCE of 19.1% and a stellar 3-year median ROE of 27% [E10, E12, E19]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a stark intrinsic value of Rs 134 per share against the current market price of Rs 32.8, leaving an enormous margin of safety of 75.4% [E33, E34]. The reverse DCF model confirms this mispricing, indicating that today's price incorrectly assumes a negative 1.5% earnings growth [E35]. Financially, the company operates from a position of immense strength with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, making it almost entirely debt-free [E28, E38]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -4.09 Cr in Mar 2026 and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E25, E40].

Stanbik Agro Ltd is trading at a modest P/E of 10 [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 1.31x against a book value of ₹ 25.0 [E2], while offering an extraordinary margin of safety of 75.4% based on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 134 per share compared to its market price of ₹ 32.8 [E33, E34]. The business demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line expansion, boasting a 3-year compounded sales growth of 63% [E14], a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 64% [E15], and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 62% [E16]. Profitability and capital efficiency are exceptionally robust, underscored by a strong 3-year median return on equity of 27.0% [E39], an ROCE of 14.34% outperforming the sector benchmark of 8.26% [E10], and an ROE of 13.07% that easily eclipses the sector benchmark of -20.7% [E9]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E28, E38], and a reverse DCF highlights that today's market price absurdly implies negative earnings growth of -1.5% [E35]. Conceded: operating cash flow for Mar 2026 is negative at Rs -4.09 Cr [E25] and the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

The bull leans heavily on a cheap P/E of 10 [E1] and an intrinsic value of ₹ 134 [E33], but ignores the severe cash generation crisis where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -4.09 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -4.14 Cr in Mar 2026 [E25, E26]. Conceded: the company boasts a 3-year compounded sales growth of 63% and profit growth of 62% [E14, E16], alongside a clean debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E28]. However, that reported earnings expansion is completely disconnected from reality when cash conversion is -0.94x and operating cash flow represents -76% of operating profit [E24, E27]. Furthermore, promoters have dumped a massive 30.40 percentage points of their stake, slashing holdings from 98.92% in Dec 2025 to 68.52% in Jun 2026 [E31]. The bull highlights an attractive ROE track record and return metrics [E9, E10, E39], yet the company refuses to pay out a single rupee in dividends despite reported profits [E4, E40], coupled with a flagged low tax rate [E41] and inconsistent operating margins over the last two periods [E22, E23].
